note: Raziyya taught as Iltutmish's daughter who became Sultan in 1236 and styled herself the Sultan's daughter on coins/inscriptions (claims c13, c15) — i.e. not a purchased slave. Balban's own slave origin, needed to eliminate all options, is now also taught in s2 (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 3: Balban was sold to Iltutmish).

Now taught in s8: Barani is the author of Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi (NIOS 315 Lesson 9), and the book is the history of the Delhi Sultanate from Balban to Firoz Shah Tughlaq (e-PG Pathshala, Sources for the Study of Indian History).

Still untaught: earliest contact of Islam with India (bank key: Arab merchants of the Malabar coast) is pre-Sultanate scope. NIOS Lesson 9 covers the Arab conquest of Sindh (AD 712) but not the merchant-contact key; no fetched authorised source supports it.

Now taught in s4: Alauddin led the first Turkish expedition to southern India in AD 1294 and plundered Devagiri, during Jalaluddin Khalji's reign (NIOS 315 Lesson 9). The bank key (Jalaluddin Khalji) is flagged doubtful_key in the bank; the chapter teaches the sourced fact, which matches the reign attribution.

Now taught in s4: Muhammad Tughlaq transferred the capital from Delhi to Deogir, renamed Daulatabad (NIOS 315 Lesson 9); Barani's stated reason — its central location — and the scheme's failure are taught, with Ibn Battuta's 1330 description of Delhi (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 12).
Kitab-ul-Hind by Al-Biruni — taught in s5 with the 80-chapter description (claim c45).
Now taught in s2: the Turkan-i Chihilgani ('Forty') was created by Iltutmish and eliminated/destroyed by Balban (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 3; NIOS 315 Lesson 9; e-PG Pathshala Slave Dynasty module).

Now taught in s3: Alauddin Khalji's market/price control — fixed prices to maintain a large army, three Delhi markets (Mandi, Sarai Adl, horses/slaves/cattle) under the Shahna-i-Mandi (NIOS 315 Lesson 9).

Now taught in s8: the Qutb Minar's foundation was laid by Qutbuddin Aibak but it was completed by Iltutmish (completed 1231) (e-PG Pathshala, Slave Dynasty and Sayyid-Lodi modules; IGNOU Unit 17 dates the building 1199–1235). The bank marks this alt mapping OUT_OF_SCOPE; it is now covered here.
Now taught in s4: Malik Kafur, captured in the Gujarat campaign, became Alauddin's trusted commander and led the invasions of South India (NIOS 315 Lesson 9).
Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq — taught in s5 (arrival 1333, appointed qazi of Delhi; claims c49, c50).

Now taught: Aibak was Ghori's slave general (NIOS 315 Lesson 9), Iltutmish was a slave and son-in-law of Aibak (e-PG Pathshala), Balban was sold to Iltutmish (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 3) — while Alauddin was Jalaluddin's nephew who killed him and seized the throne in 1296 (IGNOU Unit 3), i.e. not a slave. Reinforced by practice question q70.
Khajuraho temples / Alberuni statement pair — primary chapter HIS-09. Al-Biruni is taught here (s5), but the Khajuraho link is not in the fetched sources. Unchanged.

Now taught in s1: khutba defined as the formal Friday sermon in which the Sultan's name was mentioned as head of the community; khutba and sikka were attributes of sovereignty (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 3). Alt chapter HIS-13 also maps this PYQ.

Now taught in s3: Iltutmish brought the provinces under a uniform administrative system through iqtas (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 4) and gave shape to the iqta system (NIOS 315 Lesson 9) — the introduction/attribution to Iltutmish is now explicit.

Now taught in s7: Bakhtiyar Khalji's invasion of Bengal at the end of the 12th century and Lakshman Sen's flight from Nadia marked the beginning of Muslim rule in Bengal (IGNOU EHI-03 Block 3, §9.8; NIOS 315 Lesson 9).

Now taught in s3: Iltutmish organised the iqta system, a centrally recruited/paid/administered army, and uniform coinage — silver tanka and copper jital (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 4; NIOS 315 Lesson 9; e-PG Pathshala).

Monuments pair mismatch (bank key flagged doubtful_key). Sultanate architecture basics are now taught in s8 (Qutb Minar, Alai Darwaza, Quwwat-ul Islam), but the specific mismatched pair in this bank question could not be verified from the fetched authorised sources; left untaught rather than guessed.
Chronology of dynasties (Ilbari, Khilji, Tughluq, Lodi) — the dynasty sequence is taught in s1 from the NCERT ruler table (claims c04, c05, c37).
Now taught in s8: Amir Khusrau earned the title Tut-i-Hind, the parrot of India (e-PG Pathshala, Sayyid-Lodi / Salient Features module).

Adina Mosque built by Sikandar Shah — still untaught: no fetched authorised source (NCERT, IGNOU BHIC-107/EHI units, NIOS 315, e-PG Pathshala) covers the Adina Mosque or Sikandar Shah of Bengal. The gap is disclosed to students in the s7 bengal box.

Now taught in s4: Balban's NW frontier policy — Mongol preoccupation, forts of Sunam and Bhatinda strengthened, never leaving Delhi, Prince Muhammad killed in 1285 (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 4; e-PG Pathshala).
Now taught in s1: Ibrahim Lodi named as the last Sultan of Delhi, defeated by Babur in AD 1526 (NIOS 315 Lesson 9, introduction).
Now taught in s4: the first Deccan expeditions under Alauddin — Devagiri 1294 and the southern expeditions under Malik Kafur (NIOS 315 Lesson 9).
Now taught in s3: Alauddin Khalji firmly established the practice of payment of salaries in cash to the soldiers (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 4, §4.3.1).

Now taught in s4: Firuz Tughluq's fort towns — Hissar Firuza, Fatehabad, Firozabad, Jaunpur (IGNOU BHIC-107 Unit 12) — with Agra identified as Sikandar Lodi's capital (1504, e-PG Pathshala) for eliminating the standard odd-one-out. Reinforced by practice question q69.

Roop Goswami and Sanatan Goswami in the court of Hussain Shah — primary chapter HIS-12; no fetched authorised source for this chapter covers them. Hussain Shah's reign and Chaitanya's movement are now taught in s7, but the Goswamis are not. Gap disclosed in the s7 bengal box.

Alauddin abolished the iqta system (bank key flagged doubtful_key) — the fetched sources say the opposite direction: iqta service conditions were rigorously imposed under Alauddin (c28) and he firmly established cash salaries (IGNOU Unit 4). The key/text tension is now explicitly flagged to students in the s3 exam_note box; the key itself is not taught.
Gunaraj Khan title given to Maladhar Basu — still untaught: no fetched authorised source covers Bengal Sultanate literary personalities. Gap disclosed in the s7 bengal box.

Now taught in s8: Amir Khusrau is credited with having invented the sitar (e-PG Pathshala) — taught together with the source's own caveat 'though we have no evidence of it', flagged in the s8 exam_note box; the bank key is Amir Khusrau.
Adina Mosque is at Pandua — still untaught: no fetched authorised source covers the Adina Mosque/Pandua. Gap disclosed in the s7 bengal box.
Now taught in s3: Alauddin Khalji's market control (NIOS 315 Lesson 9) — same cluster as WBCS 2018 Q176.
